findings.reason: a coordinator working the plan from its §7 build order and open followups never dispatches §8, and nothing holds §8 behind the store-function precondition it shares with its siblings, so it can start before the function it changes exists.
findings.text: the gate `g-erkc-1` gates `s3,s4,s5` but not `s8`; §8 states its change "belongs in `plan_review_path` and `store_plan_review`", the same store function the gate's required-evidence measure protects, so §8 depends on the same `store_delivered_reviews` precondition the gate enforces for §3/§4/§5 and is outside it. No followup names §8 either: `f-erkc-001`…`f-erkc-005` cover §2/§3/§5/§4 and §7 names only §2/§6/§3/§5/§4.

findings.reason: a node closing §4 on this done-when cannot show its guard fires; the raw-report retention pass and the lifecycle derivation could both be inert and the stated assertions still hold.
findings.text: §4's done-when carries no negative control: it asserts the lifecycle is derived, a shift to landed is observed, `declined_recurrence` reads the archive, the summary reproduces §1's figure, and retention prints removals, but names no mutation under which the suite must go red; every landed section in this plan (comments at plan.html:188, 194, 203, 209, 218) states one that failed `EXIT=1`.

findings.reason: a node dispatched for change (1) cannot be closed on the combined done-when (the census-zero and second-pass-zero clauses belong to change (2)), so the section is neither reviewable nor closeable on one verdict.
findings.text: §8 declares two deliverables — (1) a review-run-keyed store path and (2) an import of delivered reports no record carries — as "Two changes, as two nodes", yet the section carries one `data-status` and one done-when paragraph covering both changes.

findings.reason: the mechanism as written breaks the reader it claims keeps working, sending a node to rename the store path without repointing the readers that enumerate it.
findings.text: §8's change (1) renames the staging file to be keyed by review run ("two reviews of one plan version never share a staging file") and asserts "Readers that key on the version still read the newest", but the version-keyed reader `plan_review._candidate_paths` enumerates the staging tree only by the literal globs `plan-<slug>.v<N>.json` and `plan-<slug>.v<N>.at-*.json`, which a run-keyed staging filename does not match; the plan names no reader change to keep them reading, and the delivered reports §8 targets are not committed until the import runs, so the staging reader is the one that must still see them.
